key_insight: A spectral interface-evolution model captures fluid-fluid displacement and energy dissipation in rough fractures beyond the quasistatic limit, linking microscale Haines jumps to macroscale hysteresis.
engineering_relevance: This provides a computationally efficient way to predict retention hysteresis and dissipation in heterogeneous porous and fractured media, with direct relevance to flow control and upscaling.
method: Developed a spectral computational approach for interface evolution and dissipation.
Validated against CFD simulations and experiments.
Applied the model to a single defect and random roughness to probe multiscale dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by comparison with CFD and experiments, and demonstrates dynamics spanning many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a model rough Hele-Shaw fracture, so extending it to fully realistic 3D porous systems may require additional assumptions and validation.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
